exercises.title: Read input and correct an arithmetic operation
exercises.goal: Read one integer and print that value plus two. Predict the output before changing the program.
hints: The input is already read and converted correctly. Compare the required operation with the expression passed to printLine.
Try input 5 by hand: the current program produces 3, not 7.
Use addition rather than subtraction in value - 2.
exercises.transfer: Implement the same input conversion and operation in Java or TypeScript, and explain how invalid input is handled.

exercises.title: Enforce both budget conditions
exercises.goal: Read an amount and a budget in integer minor units. Print APPROVE only when the amount is positive and fits the budget; otherwise print REJECT.
hints: Two independent requirements must both hold, not just either requirement.
An amount larger than the budget is still positive. Does the current condition admit it?
Join the comparisons with &&.
exercises.transfer: Write the same predicate in Java. Explain why money is represented in integer minor units rather than floating point.

exercises.title: Test the boundary, not just typical inputs
exercises.goal: Read an age. Print ELIGIBLE for ages at least 18, and INELIGIBLE otherwise.
hints: Test one value below the boundary, the boundary itself, and one above it.
The requirement includes age 18. The current comparison does not.
The operator for greater than or equal is >=.
exercises.transfer: Add a boundary-focused unit test in a mainstream test framework and describe why it catches the bug.

exercises.title: Keep array access inside its bounds
exercises.goal: Read an index into [10, 20, 30]. Print the selected value for a valid index, or INVALID otherwise.
hints: Arrays start at index zero. Count the valid indices for three elements.
The length is 3, but the final valid index is 2.
Require index < arrayLength(values), retaining the nonnegative check.
exercises.transfer: Explain how bounds failures surface in Java arrays and how an explicit guard changes the user-facing result.

exercises.title: Include every required loop iteration
exercises.goal: For an input from 0 through 10, print the sum of integers from 1 through the input, inclusive.
hints: Trace the value and total columns for input 1 before using a larger input.
The current loop stops before adding limit.
Use an inclusive upper-bound comparison in the loop condition.
exercises.transfer: Port the loop to TypeScript and write down a loop invariant about total.

exercises.title: Separate a reusable calculation from input handling
exercises.goal: Read an amount and a fixed fee, then print their sum using the total function.
hints: The input-handling method delegates the calculation. Fix the calculation where it is defined.
A fixed fee is added once, not multiplied by the amount.
Return amount + fee from total.
exercises.transfer: Create a pure Java function with the same signature and demonstrate a test that does not read stdin.

exercises.title: Normalize input deliberately
exercises.goal: Read a line, remove surrounding spaces, and print it in uppercase.
hints: Capitalization and whitespace removal are separate transformations.
Observe the leading/trailing spaces for input ' hello '.
Call value.trim().toUpperCase().
exercises.transfer: Port normalization to JavaScript and explain why validation should still happen after normalization.

exercises.title: Handle conversion failure explicitly
exercises.goal: Read a line. Print its integer value if conversion succeeds; print INVALID if conversion throws.
hints: The conversion can fail before printLine runs. Choose where the error boundary belongs.
Use try around the conversion and success output, then catch the failure.
A catch (e) block can print INVALID; do not print the success value after a failed conversion.
exercises.transfer: Implement the same error boundary in Java and explain what failures should not be hidden.

exercises.title: Update state instead of replacing it
exercises.goal: Read an initial balance and a deposit. Print the new balance after depositing into a Counter instance.
hints: The constructor establishes the starting balance. Deposit should preserve it.
For initial 10 and deposit 5, replacement yields 5 but accumulation yields 15.
Assign this.balance + amount back to this.balance.
exercises.transfer: Port the class to Java and distinguish object state from local variables and static fields.

exercises.title: Compose a small business rule
exercises.goal: Read amount, budget, requester and approver on four lines. Approve only a positive affordable amount with a different approver. Print APPROVE or REJECT.
hints: A numerical budget check does not establish who is authorized to approve.
The missing rule is separation of requester and approver identities.
Add requester != approver to the conjunction; keep both numerical checks.
exercises.transfer: Implement the rule in Java or TypeScript using the same cases. Explain why real authorization must use trusted identities from the host, not arbitrary input text.
